summary:
Planetary Analog Explorer is an interactive web app we built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It compares real places on Earth, called terrestrial analogs, with environments on the Moon, Mars, and other worlds. It covers 10 Earth field sites, including Egypt’s Black and White Deserts, and 10 planetary targets. Users compare them across 6 scientific dimensions: geology, terrain, climate, water, and exploration science.

It addresses the challenge by turning scattered research papers into one clear, searchable, visual tool. Every comparison explains what is similar and what the scientific limits are, so users don’t mistake an analog for an exact copy of another world. This matters because space agencies use Earth analogs to train astronauts, and plan missions, and the public should be able to understand that work.
details:
OUT OF THE ORBIT is an interactive website that helps people explore planet Earth and compare its natural places (like deserts, ice valleys, and caves) with places on the Moon and Mars. It shows what Earth can teach us about exploring space.

How It Works:

Earth & Space Guides: Users can browse through cards and profiles of real places on Earth and other worlds, complete with photos and descriptions.

Deep Comparison Tool: Users can pick an Earth location (like a desert) and a space target (like Mars) to compare them side-by-side across six areas (such as terrain, weather, water, and geology).

Interactive Space Simulator: A live animated canvas lets users watch a mini solar system model move and adjust the speed.

Main Goals and Benefits:

Simple Learning: It makes space science easy to understand for everyone—no science background needed.

Honest Science: It teaches users that looking similar doesn't mean two places are identical. It clearly explains where comparisons work and where they break down (like differences in gravity or air).

Space Prep: It shows how studying Earth helps scientists test equipment, planetary rover landings, and search for resources.

Tools and Technologies Used

Languages: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Graphics:HTML5 Canvas and SVG for animations and visual art.
